newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania seeks good relations with Russia.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania seeks good relations with Russia.

text.p: Lithuanian independence leader Vytautas Landsbergis appealed on Saturday for Moscow's understanding of Lithuania's drive for NATO and European Union membership.
"Russia should understand that Lithuania wants security guarantees that lead to stability and allow for the creation of well-being," Landsbergis told a conference on Lithuanian-Russian relations.

Russia is deeply opposed to the expansion of NATO to include its old Cold War satellites and is especially sensitive about the Baltic states, which were part of the former Soviet empire and once a key strategic part of its defence system.

Landsbergis, who made a political comeback when his Homeland Union party won 70 of the 141 seats in parliament in recent elections, spearheaded Lithuania's bid for independence from the former Soviet Union in 1990.
The Homeland Union will form the backbone of the new government and Landsbergis is set to be speaker of the new parliament. He is expected to fight for the presidency in 1998.
Often critical of Russia in the past due to suspicions that some in the Moscow leadership harboured imperialist ambitions, Landsbergis adopted a more conciliatory tone.
"We would like not only good and fruitful relations but even to be a model for relations between big and small countries as a whole," he said.
"We have chosen friendship and the principle of equal partnership for relations with Russia. There will be no problems between the two nations if politicians do not create artificial ones."
